5  THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
Both the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation ('KSRTC' for short) as well as the claimants are in appeal.

2. The KSRTC is in appeal contending that the attribution of negligence only to the extent of 20% on the rider of the motor-cycle was incorrect, since admittedly there were three people travelling in the bike.
3. On the other hand, the claimants contend that merely because three people were traveling in the two- wheeler, that would not lead to an inference that they had contributed to the accident.

4. It is contended that though no evidence is adduced to indicate that the riding of the motor-cycle,
in which three people were travelling, was the cause for the accident and therefore, it is contended that the attribution of 20% negligence is incorrect.
It is also contended that the assessment of disability and the sums awarded by the Tribunal are on the lower side.
5. As far as negligence is concerned, no doubt, the evidence on record indicates that three people were riding the bike at the time of the accident.
The fact also remains that the charge-sheet was lodged only against the driver of the KSRTC bus.

Even according to the Tribunal, the rider of the motor cycle did not in any way contribute to the accident but it merely observes that because three people were travelling in the bike, there is every chance of the rider of the motor cycle losing control over the motor- cycle.
6. In my view, such reasoning cannot justify the attribution of the negligence on the rider of the motor- cycle.

Unless there is clear and clinching evidence to indicate that the rider of the motor-cycle had contributed to the accident, or the fact that three people riding the motor-cycle caused the accident, the Tribunal could not have attributed 20% negligence on the rider of the motor- cycle.
7. Consequently, the finding of the Tribunal as regards the negligence is set aside.
It is held that the driver of the KSRTC bus was negligent in causing the accident and as such, the KSRTC is liable to pay the entire compensation.

The medical evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered 54%

10.
The evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered fracture of the distal right femur, apart from an open fracture of the neck right of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd meta-tarsal bone.
In the light of the amount of fracture that the claimant had suffered, it would be appropriate to determine the whole body disability of the claimant at 20% as against 18% determined by the Tribunal.

11. The Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/-
notionally and has proceeded to add 50% of the same as future prospects.

In my view,
- 10 - since there was no evidence to ascertain the actual income, the sum of Rs.9,000/- determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accidents of the year 2015 will have to be applied.

12. Since the claimant has suffered 20% permanent physical disability to the whole body and was aged about 27 years as on the date of the accident, 40% of the same (Rs.3,600/-) is required to be added to the said income as future prospects, as per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others - (2017) 16 SCC 680, and the resultant income would be Rs.12,600/-.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering.

In my view, since the claimant has sustained severe fractures and suffered 20% disability, it would be just and appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering as against Rs.20,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
